language.label: Language
guide.step1: Connect the Mac and DJI controller to the same Wi-Fi or hotspot.
guide.step2: Copy the RTMP address below into DJI Fly and start streaming.
guide.step3: When the preview appears, enable the virtual camera once and approve it in macOS if asked.
guide.step4: Start the virtual camera, then open TikTok LIVE Studio.
guide.step5: Select DJI Live Bridge Camera, set its audio capture to None, choose one microphone, then click Go Live.
warning.ipChanged: LAN IP changed. Update the RTMP address in DJI Fly before restarting the livestream.
preview.reason.transcodeReady: Preview-only H.264 + Opus transcode is ready; ingest and production remain independent.
preview.reason.aacNotice: Direct WHEP video is connected. AAC is not carried to the browser preview; enable the H.264 + Opus fallback when preview audio is required.
preview.reason.failed: The preview connection failed. See technical details below.
recording.nativeHelp: Records the real /production mix when live, otherwise the direct /drone stream.
destination.removeConfirm: Remove this destination and its saved stream key?
camera.liveStudioHelp: Choose “{device}” as the Camera source, set that source's Audio capture to None, and choose one microphone from LIVE Studio's main audio control. Go Live remains manual.
camera.detail.notInstalled: The signed camera extension is not installed
camera.detail.updateReady: A camera extension update is ready. Enable it to replace the active version.
camera.detail.enabled: DJI Live Bridge Camera is enabled by macOS
camera.detail.waitingApproval: Camera extension activation is waiting for macOS approval
camera.detail.notBundled: This app bundle does not contain the camera extension
camera.detail.moveToApplications: Move DJI Live Bridge.app to /Applications before enabling the camera
camera.detail.notEnabled: Camera extension is bundled but not enabled
camera.detail.activationRequested: Activation requested. Approve DJI Live Bridge Camera in System Settings if macOS asks.
camera.detail.feedReady: Portrait video is ready. DJI Live Bridge audio is disabled; select one microphone only in TikTok LIVE Studio.
camera.detail.feedStopped: Camera extension is enabled; the video feed is stopped
obs.help: Use OBS only when you need its scene system, filters, recording or Virtual Camera. It is not required for Direct RTMP.

diagnostics.action.lan: Connect the Mac and DJI RC 2 to the same LAN or hotspot, then select the interface.
diagnostics.action.mediamtx: Check ports 1935, 8554, 8889 and 9997, then reinstall the pinned sidecar if needed.
diagnostics.action.publisher: Start RTMP streaming to the displayed URL.
diagnostics.action.ffmpeg: Install an FFmpeg build that includes H.264 and Opus encoders.
diagnostics.action.productionCapabilitie: Install a supported FFmpeg build; OBS remains an optional fallback.
diagnostics.action.productionRoute: Prepare production and explicitly press START LIVE; if an error is shown, verify the destination URL and key.
diagnostics.action.camera: Use a signed build from /Applications and allow the camera extension in System Settings when requested.
diagnostics.action.obs: Optional: install or start OBS and enable its WebSocket server on port 4455.
diagnostics.action.microphone: Connect or enable a microphone. macOS requests permission only when built-in commentary capture is used.
diagnostics.action.tiktok: Open the current official TikTok download page from the destination panel.

errors.action.network: Select an active LAN interface and verify Local Network permission.
errors.action.process: Open Diagnostics and inspect the supervised process status.
errors.action.mediamtx: Verify local port availability and reinstall the pinned MediaMTX sidecar if needed.
errors.action.ffmpeg: Install a supported FFmpeg build and run Diagnostics again.
errors.action.obs: Start OBS, enable obs-websocket, and verify the host, port, and password.
errors.action.virtualCamera: Install the app in /Applications, enable the camera in System Settings, then retry.
errors.action.transition: Return to the previous workflow step and retry.
errors.action.unsupported: Complete this step manually in the destination application.
errors.action.validation: Correct the highlighted value and retry.
errors.action.io: Check file permissions and available disk space.
errors.action.http: Verify that the local service and loopback port are available.
errors.action.serialization: Reset the affected local setting and retry.
s1.title: Connect your drone
s1.help: In DJI Fly open GO FLY → ••• → Transmission → Live Streaming Platforms → RTMP and paste this address. The Mac and the controller must be on the same Wi-Fi or hotspot.
s2.title: Where do you want to stream?
s2.name: Name (optional)
s2.keyKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved key
s2.help.Instagram: On instagram.com: Create (+) → Live video. Copy the “Stream URL” and “Stream key” into the fields below. Instagram gives a new key for every live session.
s2.help.TikTok: In TikTok LIVE Center or LIVE Studio, open the stream key screen and copy the Server URL and Stream key. Your account needs RTMP access.
s2.help.Custom: Paste the RTMP / RTMPS server address and stream key your platform gives you.
s2.igKeyNote: Instagram creates a new key for each broadcast. Update the key before you go live.
s3.title: Picture and sound
s3.portraitHint: Instagram and TikTok expect vertical video.
go.title: Go live
go.ready: Everything is ready. Press the button to start.
go.igReminder: Now open Instagram and press “Go live” there. Your stream becomes public only after that.
go.tiktokReminder: Check TikTok LIVE Center; the stream may need to be started there too.
go.partial: One destination failed; the others are still live.
camera.tabHelp: Only needed if you stream through the TikTok LIVE Studio app. Instagram does not need this.
advanced.tabHelp: Recording, stream metrics, OBS and system checks.
theme.label: Theme
camera.rebootTitle: macOS will finish enabling the virtual camera after a restart.
camera.rebootAction: Restart the Mac, open DJI Live Bridge and press Start Virtual Camera again.

ffmpeg.title: FFmpeg could not be found
ffmpeg.help: DJI Live Bridge ships with FFmpeg, so this normally never appears. If the app bundle was altered, you can install FFmpeg separately.
ffmpeg.installing: Installing… this can take a few minutes
ffmpeg.needBrew: Homebrew was not found. FFmpeg is installed through Homebrew, so install that first and come back — the button will then do the rest.
